scenarios.name: Geopolitical De-escalation
scenarios.description: Reduced tensions in major conflicts (e.g., Middle East, Ukraine) leading to stabilized energy prices and improved global trade flows.

impacts.explanation: Lower energy prices reduce input costs for goods and services.
Improved trade relations reduce deficit growth.

scenarios.reasoning: Base rates from past conflict resolutions suggest moderate likelihood of de-escalation. Balances inside view (current military spending) with outside view (global diplomacy trends).
tetlockCommandments: Strive to distinguish as many degrees of doubt as the problem permits

scenarios.name: Persistent Trade Wars
scenarios.description: Escalation of US-China trade tensions with new tariffs and supply chain fragmentation.

impacts.explanation: Higher import costs from retaliatory tariffs.
Disrupted global supply chains reduce manufacturing output.

scenarios.reasoning: Current tariff trends and geopolitical rivalries increase probability. Contradicts outside view of trade globalization but aligns with rising protectionism signals.
tetlockCommandments: Break seemingly intractable problems into tractable sub-problems

scenarios.name: Fed Rate Cut Cycle
scenarios.description: Federal Reserve lowers rates due to persistently low unemployment and cooling inflation.

impacts.explanation: Direct policy action reducing borrowing costs.
Lower mortgage rates stimulate residential construction.

scenarios.reasoning: outside view of historical Fed behavior in similar economic conditions suggests high probability. Requires balancing underconfidence in immediate inflation concerns.
tetlockCommandments: Strike the right balance between under- and overreacting to evidence

scenarios.name: Energy Price Spike
scenarios.description: Sudden increase in oil/gas prices due to Middle East instability or supply disruptions.

impacts.explanation: Higher energy costs propagate through economy.
Reduced consumer spending on energy-intensive goods.

scenarios.reasoning: Current geopolitical uncertainties in oil-producing regions increase risk. Combines inside view (recent price volatility) with outside view (historical energy crisis patterns).
tetlockCommandments: Look for the clashing causal forces at work in each problem

scenarios.name: Tech Sector Crash
scenarios.description: -collapse of major US tech stocks due to AI investment disappointments or regulatory crackdowns.

impacts.explanation: Reduced capital expenditure in tech manufacturing.

scenarios.reasoning: underestimated potential for sector-specific shocks in current meta-narrative. Requires granular analysis of tech industry vulnerabilities.
tetlockCommandments: Triage - Focus on questions where careful thinking pays off

scenarios.name: Housing Market Recovery
scenarios.description: Federal stimulus programs and rate cuts boost housing construction and sales.

impacts.explanation: Direct policy support for residential building.

scenarios.reasoning: low probability but possible if Fed demonstrates commitment to rate cuts. Balances against outside view of current housing affordability challenges.
tetlockCommandments: Strike the right balance between under- and overconfidence

methodology: Scenario analysis with probabilities derived from Tetlock pillars (outside views, granular analysis) and commandments (error-balancing, probabilistic thinking). Weighted forecasts combine scenario impacts proportionally.
geopoliticalSummary: Moderate conflict risks in Middle East and Eastern Europe, but no imminent escalation to major wars. Trade tensions remain between US and China.
geoeconomicSummary: Global supply chains fragmented by trade wars, energy prices volatile due to geopolitical factors. US trade deficit accelerating.
currentEventsSummary: Inflation cooling to 3.46% despite energy price pressures. Fed maintains rates as unemployment stays low. Housing starts remain depressed.
